Having built trust and routines, the 2025/6 year began with a broader and more ambitious curriculum for all of our students, and students were either baselined or progress checked in October (to ensure they had settled into the new school year and to ensure accurate and reliable assessment).
In June 2024 the students were ready for academic baselining in English, Maths, Science, Art, Humanities, Cooking and PE.
I have a firm belief that every child deserves the opportunity to thrive, and I am committed to delivering a broad, ambitious curriculum that fosters a lifelong love of learning.

A specialist school in Princes Risborough for young people aged 11- 18 with a range of complex needs.
Welcome to Red Kite School
Red Kite School is an independent specialist school in Princes Risborough for students aged 11 – 18 who have a range of complex needs, including social, emotional and mental health (SEMH), communication and interaction and associated challenging behaviour.
To help you navigate this website, either follow the green buttons at the end of each page or use the drop down menu at the top.
Curriculum
Pupils at Red Kite School will have access to an adapted curriculum which takes account of the National Curriculum as well as being relevant to individual needs.
The underlying belief that governs development is that learning should be useful, relevant and enjoyable.
Clinical
As well as delivering the best possible education, we also have access to a clinical team who provide care and therapy to benefit our pupils.
Red Kite School offers a therapeutic educational approach with a staff team dedicated and determined to support every individual.
Newsletters
We’re proud to share what makes our school so special. Our newsletters celebrate the achievements, events and everyday moments that bring our community to life.
Read our latest newsletters to see what we’ve been up to.
© OFG Education 2026

Ofsted Report Card February 2026
10427410 – Red Kite School – 150899 Final (2)Parents and Carers
The relationships we have with parents and carers of the students we educate and care for are really important. We are committed to providing the expert ongoing support they need at every stage of their partnership with us.
Effective home-school relationships help our students meet our mission statement and school motto:
Red Kite School strives to equip students with the skills, knowledge and citizenship skills to be successful in their future.
Respect – Responsibility – Resilience
Red Kite School commits to investing in the home-school relationship. This includes:
Regular contact from the Form Tutor and when necessary other members of staff
Termly parent-student-school events, including charity events
Annual reviews for EHCPs
Progress updates / reports
Parent consultation events.
Should you have any questions, please do not hesitate in contacting your child’s Form Tutor or when necessary other members of staff.
Pupil Premium Statement
Pupil Premium funding is incorporated into the Red Kite School day fees.
Academic Year 2024-2025 – Number of formal complaints = 1 (updated 31-7-25).
Please see the Complaints Policy for more details, including publishing complaints.
Positive Correspondence
“Good evening, I hope you are well.
I want to let you know what a great day X has had.
Please pass on to X how proud we are of him today. He has demonstrated our Red Kite values of Respect, Resilience and Responsibility .
Please do not hesitate to contact me with any question about X’s plan or his new form.
Red Kite’s Specialist setting has offered X everything that she needs to help her maintain being regulated.
Your execution in the way you deliver her individual special needs is precise. You notice everything about her,
for example if she likes kinetic sand you have offered to get her favourite colour, you have given her choices
and this has had a positive effect her eating. She now likes to eat breakfast at home as you offered so many
alternatives, she felt comfortable enough to try something new. You do not pressure her and this had made
her flourish. I can see that she will be doing many amazing things at this school. You have also made me as a
parent very welcome, all your staff that I have met are very welcoming and most importantly your interested
and you listen to us…”
“Michael, it looks like the school has made three months progress in three weeks since I was last here.”
“I absolutely love working here.”
“X’s grandfather said during our network meeting yesterday: ‘X has come along way this year and this is all down to school, she would not be where she is now if it was not for Red Kite’
Designated Safeguarding Lead
X and I were talking today after school and just to say thanks so much for your support, as always.
Thank you so much for your email and for your lovely words about X… We really enjoyed the coffee morning, it’s such a lovely event to put on, it’s particularly good for us parents to come in and see everything they have done and continue to do. I was so thrilled with her achievements and she was super keen to show her dad! I agree this feels like a really positive step forward…Thanks again for your continued support.
I just wanted to drop you a quick note to say a proper thank you — I haven’t had the chance to catch you in person, but I really didn’t want to let it go unsaid.
You’ve done such a brilliant job helping to shape Red Kite into an even better place to work, and I really appreciate everything you’ve put into that. In particular, I think the fortnightly newsletter is a fantastic addition. It’s such a great way to shine a light on all the everyday wins happening around the school — and it brings such a positive buzz with it. I know these things don’t just magically happen, so thank you for all the effort it’s taken to get it going. I love that potential students and families can get an idea of the Red Kite day looks like week to week through the flyer.
I got to have a good chat with a parent during the coffee morning, and she spoke very positively of the Newsletter, saying how she loved to see what the students got up to and enjoyed the successes being shared on there.
Teacher (Red Kite School)
Article in OFG company bulletin
“Red Kite School Reflect on Action Packed First Year
Since opening in September, the fun at Red Kite School has not stopped. From enlightening trips including museum visits, a Silverstone STEM careers event, local walks and games in the park, to coffee mornings, bake-offs, a gardening club and drama workshops onsite, pupils have had lots of ways to explore their unique interests.
Assistant Headteacher, Lucy Metcalfe, shared ‘Alongside this packed agenda, we’ve developed sensory rooms to deliver a light and calming space, and focused on improving our curriculum so that every child can enjoy school. Our team has done a huge amount of work this year, which is reflected in our thriving, brilliant community, with pupils making great progress.’”
It was so great to meet you and Alice yesterday. Thanks for giving us such a warm welcome. X loved her visit and is so excited to start on Monday (which is nothing short of a miracle!).
Best wishes and enjoy your weekend.”
Thank you so much for these reports it’s so lovely to get a positive report.
X is loving being at Red kite. We were talking on the way home from school today I said that I thinks he’s finally found his place, X agreed and said it was the best school he’s ever been to.
Thank you and all the staff for making X feel so comfortable and happy at school!”
I am pleased to say X has really settled and made a great start. X is making excellent progress. She is currently on track to go full time from 20-10-25.
Michael Davis (Red Kite School)
This is really great news and a testament to the provision you provide. Thank you so much for the update.
Senior SEN Officer Oxfordshire County
Tribunals, Resolutions and Compliance (SEND)
Just to state what is perhaps obvious, we continue to be delighted with X’s progress at Red Kite and have nothing but praise for you and your staff in what you are doing for her. So thank you!”
“I loved the website, especially the newsletter. It shows how enjoyable and rewarding it must be to work here.”
Candidate for teaching post
Thankyou so much for this email. It’s so lovely to hear how X is doing. The change in him and his attitude to learning has changed so much since joining Red kite school. You have made learning fun for him again which he has not had in a very long time.
X loves being in your class.
Tune in to Autism Unpacked, where we’re navigating SEN together through honest conversations, expert insight, lived experience and practical advice.
We’re joined by professionals from education and therapy, alongside parents, carers and people with lived experience, to share practical insights, explore the topics that matter and help families and those supporting children and young people feel better informed.
© OFG Education 2026

Home Our Approach Safeguarding
Safeguarding
We are committed to providing the highest standards in relation to the safeguarding of the children and young people entrusted to our care.
Effective safeguarding at Red Kite School, helps students achieve our mission statement and school motto:
Red Kite School strives to equip students with the skills, knowledge and citizenship skills to be successful in their future.
Respect – Responsibility – Resilience
Red Kite School has Safeguarding and Child Protection procedures, policy documents and a training programme that incorporates Government and Policy Legislation. Staff are given a copy of the Child Protection Procedures and receive annual training from trained staff.
Parents/carers, social workers, placing authorities and other significant people are offered a copy of the Child Protection Policy. This can be found in the policy section of our website.
Red Kite School provides policy guidance, which sets out clear guidelines and expectations in the school with regard to appropriate relationships between all staff and the children. At Red Kite School, we provide a very caring and professional setting in which the children will be given full emotional support without it being detrimental to their safety and well-being. All staff are aware of their responsibilities for Safeguarding and promoting the welfare of young people.
Red Kite School has a duty of care and therefore a responsibility to pass on any child protection and safeguarding concerns to the relevant children’s social care services.
We support all students by:
We expect all staff and visitors to our school to behave in a way which ensures our children are safeguarded at all times. This includes a duty for any safeguarding concerns to be reported to the Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) Victoria Margan, or Deputy Designated Safeguarding Leads (DDSLs) Fiona Titmas or Michael Davis.
Encouraging communication, self-esteem, and self-assertiveness
Effectively tackling bullying and harassment
Protected Characteristics at Red Kite School

Home Our Approach Curriculum
Curriculum
At Red Kite School, we believe the word ‘curriculum’ should be interpreted in its widest meaning. It is every planned learning experience, both formally within a lesson and informally outside the classroom throughout the whole school day.
Accessing the curriculum enables students to aspire to our mission statement and school motto:
Red Kite School strives to equip students with the skills, knowledge and citizenship skills to be successful in their future. At Red Kite School, lessons are purposeful and are mapped against skills, knowledge and citizenship skills.
Respect – Responsibility – Resilience
Red Kite School Curriculum Intent outlines how Red Kite School strives to equip students with the:
skills, knowledge and citizenship skills, to be successful in their future.
Our ambitious and purposeful curriculum has three aims, designed to deliver a quality education for all and to help our students:
Skills: Develop confidence to tackle and understand those key life skills for success. This will include developing social communication and skills, emotional resilience and an understanding of themselves and others. Prior to joining our school, our students have often found it difficult to understand and regulate their emotions, often leading to behaviour that has challenged. This has led to them being unsuccessful in previous educational placements. It is our ambition to support and educate our students, so they are able to regulate their emotions and behave in a way that allows them to be successful in the future. We know that this will help raise self-esteem and lead to a more positive outlook on life, thus helping to ensure the best future outcomes.
Knowledge: Become successful learners so they are able to achieve the best possible outcomes, equipping them for their individual future. We know that this is different for every child that attends our school. It is our ambition to ensure ALL learners develop detailed knowledge and skills across the curriculum offer to achieve the very best outcomes. Robust baseline and ongoing assessments of each individual allows us to create adapted provision with high expectations for every student
– the staff team are unwavering in supporting students to secure their very best. The staff team will always promote the ideal of always doing your best.
Citizenship Skills: Become increasingly responsible with tolerance and respect for others and our communities. We know that key to this will be for our students to learn how to develop and maintain positive and healthy relationships so they can socialise with others well and experience lifelong friendship. Additionally, we will help raise our students understanding of the world around them whilst promoting core British Values, including democracy, the rule of law and individual liberty.
© OFG Education 2026

Home Our Approach Careers
Careers
Choosing which direction to take after leaving school is a big decision.
We want our students to experience a careers curriculum that establishes a growing knowledge and awareness of the world of work and what they, as young people, can aim for as they prepare for adulthood and post-16 transition. This includes delivering a breadth of opportunities and experiences that our students can start to build their own future pathways on. As we aim to do this, we are fully aware of the impact of the inherent difficulties our students have due to the nature of their needs and diagnosis and look to how we can start to overcome these barriers, working alongside them.
If you have any questions about careers, further education, work experience, or if you would like more information about our careers programme, please contact our Careers Lead, Lucy Metcalfe, via email lucy.metcalfe@redkiteschool.co.uk, or call 01844 885649.
The school’s Careers Advisor is Stan Flaherty, Stanley.Flaherty@ofgl.co.uk

Home About Us Clinical therapy
Clinical therapy
Red Kite School offers a therapeutic educational approach. This therapeutic approach empowers staff and students to strive towards our mission statement and school motto, namely:
Red Kite School strives to equip students with the skills, knowledge and citizenship skills to be successful in their future.
Respect – Responsibility – Resilience
Red Kite School provides a rich therapeutic offer. At Red Kite school, our students benefit from an on-site therapeutic package. This is on a three-tier basis depending on individual need. At Red Kite School, we are confident that 100% of any students’ clinical needs are being met:
Universal therapeutic offer
All students have a graduated transition in to Red Kite school
All students have access to small class-sizes with high adult to student ratios
All students have tailored access to a broad and balanced curriculum
All students have access to healthy eating options
All students have access to regulation resources, such as Zones of Regulation, sensory circuits, sensory rooms and safe spaces.
Enhanced therapeutic offer
All students have access to highly skilled staff who are Trauma Informed Practice (TIP) trained to communicate and keep students safe, appropriate to situation; our staff our upskilled by our clinical team.
Specialist therapeutic offer
Where applicable, students have access to specialist intervention to meet specific needs outlined on the EHCP and, with specialist in-house and / or external clinical therapists, such as psychotherapy, Speech and Language Therapy and Occupational Therapy.
© OFG Education 2026

Home About Us Our Team
Meet our Team
Natalie Deen – Regional Director and Chair and Safeguarding Governor
Simon Wallace – Deputy Headteacher, Quality of Education
As the Deputy Headteacher I will be focusing on Quality of Education and I am thrilled to be in such a dedicated and nurturing community at Red Kite. I have a firm belief that every child deserves the opportunity to thrive, and I am committed to delivering a broad, ambitious curriculum that fosters a lifelong love of learning. Our aim is to ensure that all students, regardless of their starting point, are given the tools, support, and inspiration they need to succeed. I’m excited to build on the school’s strengths and work with staff, families and students to secure excellent outcomes for every student at Red Kite.
Relationships and communication are key in a successful school, so please do call, email or arrange a visit if you’d like to know more.
Lucy Metcalfe- Assistant Headteacher, Behaviour & Attitudes & Personal Development & Attendance Champion
I am a creative and flexible leader who enjoys working with young people. I have been a teacher since 1998 and taught a range of subjects including Media, Expressive Arts, English, Business Studies, Geography and Home Cooking. I have gained the NASENCO and NPQSL awards and worked hard to develop my practice in a variety of settings. As SENDCO I was responsible for supporting large teams and developing the provision for our young people. This included leading on residential activities and ensuring support was timely and effective in school.
Outside of school, I am involved in my local community garden and enjoy travelling and the cinema. I am hardworking and determined to succeed, tenacious and empathetic. I enjoy coaching and mentoring and pride myself on having a positive mindset even when working in challenging situations. I love animals and have a dog and a cat. I also enjoy swimming and spending time exploring with my family and friends.
Victoria Margan – Designated Safeguarding Lead
I began my career as a teacher, working in mainstream education for 16 years. During this time, I developed a deep passion for safeguarding and supporting children and their families, which led me to retrain as a children’s social worker. This role allowed me to work closely with families during challenging times, providing vital support and guidance. I was therefore delighted to bring together my experience in both education and social care when stepping into my role as Designated Safeguarding Lead and Family Liaison Officer at Red Kite School.
Here, I am committed to creating a safe, supportive, and nurturing environment where every student feels valued and empowered to thrive. With a deep passion for supporting students with social, emotional, and mental health needs, I am committed to creating a safe, nurturing, and engaging learning environment. At Red Kite I work closely with our dedicated team to ensure that every student receives the individualized support they need to thrive—both academically and personally. Understanding that each child’s journey is unique, I take a compassionate and holistic approach, helping students build confidence, resilience, and essential life skills. My goal is to foster a sense of belonging and empowerment, equipping our students with the tools they need to succeed in education and beyond.
I am proud to be part of a school that values inclusivity, creativity, and personal growth, and I look forward to making a meaningful difference in the lives of our students.
Fiona Titmas – Pastoral Lead and Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead

Home About Us Introduction
What We Do
A brand-new specialist school in Princes Risborough for young people aged 11-18 with a range of complex needs.
Welcome to Red Kite School!
To help you navigate this website, either follow the green buttons at the end of each page or use the drop down menu at the top.
At Red Kite School our school’s aims are summarised by our Mission statement:
Red Kite School strives to equip students with the skills, knowledge and citizenship skills to be successful in their future.
At Red Kite School our ethos is summarised by our School Motto:
Respect – Responsibility – Resilience
We provide specialist education to students aged 11-18 with social, emotional and mental health needs, as well as other learning needs.
We are part of Acorn Education, the UK’s leading independent provider of specialist education for vulnerable children and young people. As part of OFG Education, we are leading our sector in setting and delivering new approaches that provide measurable outcomes for those in our care.
Previous Year’s Academic Performance
2024-2025 focussed mainly on the inclusive curriculum: building relationships with staff, getting into the routines of a school day, boosting school attendance, working towards EHCP targets (as part of Evidence for Learning) and gaining (or regaining) trust in education. During this, students showed remarkable progress in their reading. For the students who joined us in the Autumn Term 2024 the progress in the Summer Term was 27 months in reading age (equivalent to 2 years and 3 months) over the course of just one school year. In June 2024 the students were ready for academic baselining in English, Maths, Science, Art, Humanities, Cooking and PE. This informed our planning for the start of the 2025/6 academic year, including classes, adaptation and flightpaths.
Having built trust and routines, the 2025/6 year began with a broader and more ambitious curriculum for all of our students, and students were either baselined or progress checked in October (to ensure they had settled into the new school year and to ensure accurate and reliable assessment). The highlights so far this year for our students are:
1. 30 months reading progress in 9 months of school.
2. 77% of students on track or better (relative to their starting point).
3. 88% have made improvements in their reading.
4. 28% increase in lesson attendance from Summer to Autumn Term.
This shows that our system is working and our students are making considerable progress, despite many having missed a number of years of school. Students are assessed every half term (with ongoing formative assessments) to inform on future planning and adaptation.

Home About Us Clinical therapy
Clinical therapy
Red Kite School offers a therapeutic educational approach. This therapeutic approach empowers staff and students to strive towards our mission statement and school motto, namely:
Red Kite School strives to equip students with the skills, knowledge and citizenship skills to be successful in their future.
Respect – Responsibility – Resilience
Red Kite School provides a rich therapeutic offer. At Red Kite school, our students benefit from an on-site therapeutic package. This is on a three-tier basis depending on individual need. At Red Kite School, we are confident that 100% of any students’ clinical needs are being met:
Universal therapeutic offer
All students have a graduated transition in to Red Kite school
All students have access to small class-sizes with high adult to student ratios
All students have tailored access to a broad and balanced curriculum
All students have access to healthy eating options
All students have access to regulation resources, such as Zones of Regulation, sensory circuits, sensory rooms and safe spaces.
Enhanced therapeutic offer
All students have access to highly skilled staff who are Trauma Informed Practice (TIP) trained to communicate and keep students safe, appropriate to situation; our staff our upskilled by our clinical team.
Specialist therapeutic offer
Where applicable, students have access to specialist intervention to meet specific needs outlined on the EHCP and, with specialist in-house and / or external clinical therapists, such as psychotherapy, Speech and Language Therapy and Occupational Therapy.
